text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.76% today as oil prices stabilized and refining margins stayed supported. U.S. crude held around $96 per barrel while Brent stayed above $106, and with refineries running at 92.7% capacity—near full utilization—the company benefits from both steady throughput and the wider gap between crude costs and refined product prices. The competing narratives about Russian diesel flooding the market versus potential supply disruptions from geopolitical tensions created mixed signals for oil prices, but the net effect was supportive for a major U.S. refiner.

The stock's broader 20% surge over two weeks reflects a sharp reversal in refining fundamentals. Gasoline and diesel inventories remain relatively lean (204.7 million and 105.1 million barrels respectively), which tightens margins in the refiner's favor—they make money when fuel is scarce relative to crude. Geopolitical risk premiums in crude, particularly around Saudi Arabia and potential Iranian retaliation, continue to underpin oil prices despite the near-term overhang of potential Russian supply coming online.
